paragraphs.text: The analysis did not show clear, consistent trends for glioma or meningioma across its approaches. Positive findings in selected windows remain visible, but they were not consistent across methods and may reflect chance among many comparisons. The result should not become either a universal workplace safety threshold or an isolated positive headline. Related INTEROCC and INTERPHONE exposure analyses also need overlap accounting before being counted as independent replication.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 10 to 11, Discussion and Conclusion

E04-T07-R252.title: A pooled result retains its original exposure methods

paragraphs.text: The review combines studies using direct measurements, calculated fields, power-line proximity and wire codes, while considering appliance-use studies separately. Those approaches describe different exposure information. A pooled estimate does not convert a short measurement, residential distance or reported appliance use into the same personal dose history. The methodological variation and quality limitations remain part of the evidence after synthesis.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 21 to 22, Discussion and limitations

paragraphs.text: The electric-blanket analysis reports an association using older studies, and the authors explicitly caution about applying that evidence to equipment used today. Product design, operating pattern and exposure assessment belong with the interpretation. The review does not directly measure current blanket models or establish an individual prediction for a present-day user. Original studies shared with earlier pooled analyses also remain the same participants rather than additional independent evidence.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical page 18, appliance table; pages 21 to 22, appliance interpretation and limitations

paragraphs.text: The case-control comparison uses mapped distance from homes to overhead power lines. It reports higher odds of infertility among women living closer to the lines. That proximity measure is not a direct measurement of field strength at the home or energy absorbed by an individual. Other sources, time spent away from home and residential characteristics can differ even between people assigned to the same distance category.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 2 to 4, Materials and Methods, Results and Discussion

paragraphs.text: The investigators acknowledge that field measurements were not made and that the observational design does not establish the temporal or causal relationship. Selection of clinic cases and controls and other residential factors also matter. The reported association therefore does not establish that power-line fields caused infertility or that moving house would improve reproductive outcomes. A clinical recommendation would require evidence beyond this proximity comparison.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 3 to 4, distance methods and Discussion limitations

E06-T11-R191.title: Workplace patterns and a communication article

paragraphs.text: This communication explains why intermittent workplace exposure, close work near equipment and uneven fields can differ from ordinary public exposure or a controlled laboratory condition. A peak, a time average and a local exposure are different descriptions. Combining them without attention to the task and timing can hide the features that the authors want occupational research to examine.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 5 to 6, workplace exposure examples and interpretation

paragraphs.text: The article draws on prior examples and studies rather than presenting a new comparative worker cohort or pooled disease estimate. Its discussion of MRI-worker symptoms and long-term uncertainty is background evidence, not newly observed cases in this report. The call for better occupational study designs does not itself quantify a worker's individual risk. Referenced studies still need source-specific appraisal and overlap checks before clinical or causal conclusions.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical page 6, MRI/static-field context; page 12, Conclusions

E03-T06-R109.title: Call frequency and different birth outcomes

paragraphs.text: The combined birth-cohort analysis uses maternal reports of calling behavior during pregnancy. Call frequency is a behavior measure rather than a direct estimate of absorbed RF dose, particularly when call duration and operating conditions are incomplete. Some exposure reports were collected retrospectively. Combining cohorts increases the information considered, but it does not make those different measurement histories identical or create new participants beyond the contributing cohorts.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 7 to 8, Discussion and exposure limitations

paragraphs.text: More frequent calls were associated with shorter pregnancy duration, while fetal growth and birth weight did not show an association. Those endpoints should remain distinct. The authors caution that stress or residual confounding could explain the duration finding, and those possible explanations were not measured consistently enough to isolate their contributions. The result does not establish RF causation or a preventive calling rule for pregnancy.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 7 to 8, Discussion, Figure and Conclusion

E03-T05-R242.title: Cell stage, culture time and assay choice

paragraphs.text: The experiment compares mouse germ-cell models with isolated mature mouse sperm under a continuous-wave laboratory exposure. Those stages did not show the same response pattern. A mitochondrial probe signal in a precursor model should not be treated as a complete explanation for every result in mature sperm. The report concerns selected culture assays rather than exposed men or observed reproductive success.
paragraphs.locator: Main PDF physical pages 2 to 5, Methods and early Results; pages 13 to 15, Discussion

paragraphs.text: In mature sperm, fragmentation findings differed by assay and time, while selected later oxidative-DNA and motility changes were reported. Null and discordant comparisons remain relevant alongside those changes. Small biological replication and many connected contrasts limit a simple dose-response or mechanism claim. These observations do not estimate human infertility, conception risk or an appropriate phone-use duration, and scientific, numerical and human review remain pending.
paragraphs.locator: Main PDF physical pages 8 to 9 and 13 to 15, Results, Figures and Discussion

E06-T11-R185.title: Measured stations and modeled small-cell scenarios

paragraphs.text: The actual base stations measured did not meet the paper's small-cell power definitions. The investigators rescaled those measurements to selected small-cell powers and calculated typical-user and non-user scenarios. These are useful engineering estimates under stated assumptions, but they are not a representative population survey or direct measurements of every person carrying out ordinary activities near an installed small cell.
paragraphs.locator: Main PDF physical page 6, site definitions; pages 10 to 12, scenario interpretation and Discussion

paragraphs.text: The reported rescaled scenarios were below the reference levels used by the authors. That physical comparison retains the antenna geometry, traffic, averaging and separation assumptions. Close-distance coverage gaps and inconsistent nearby maximum labels require clarification before numerical reuse. A limited station sample and modeled inputs do not establish a universal distance rule or lifetime health outcome, and the study did not measure disease.
paragraphs.locator: Main PDF physical pages 9 to 12, Figures, scenario table and Discussion

E05-T09-R518.title: A defined signal comparison in a cell model

paragraphs.text: The study compares specified modulated and continuous-wave signals in neuroblastoma-cell cultures, with sham and positive-control conditions. Neither signal significantly changed the measured cell-cycle distribution or spontaneous comet-assay damage under this protocol. Prior RF exposure also did not significantly modify the response to a later menadione challenge. The result remains tied to those endpoints, observation windows and experimental arrangements.
paragraphs.locator: Main PDF physical pages 4 to 6 and 9, experimental sequence, Results and comet figure

paragraphs.text: The chemical challenge followed the RF exposure rather than occurring throughout the same interval. A negative result for that sequence does not describe every simultaneous or delayed combination. Few independent culture experiments and a transformed cell model also limit generalization to intact tissue. Methods and figure wording differ on repeated measurements, and a nonsignificant comparison does not establish universal equivalence or absence of human harm.
paragraphs.locator: Main PDF physical pages 4 to 5, protocol and Statistics; pages 9 to 10, figure wording and Discussion

E03-T05-R247.title: Selective laboratory attenuation is not clinical prevention

paragraphs.text: The same donor's semen was divided among sham, exposed and exposed-plus-Trolox conditions. Attenuation was selective across the assays: a lower concentration improved some comparisons, while a higher concentration was not uniformly more favorable. The mitochondrial measures were not rescued. These details qualify a broad protection narrative and do not show that increasing an antioxidant concentration necessarily improves the result.
paragraphs.locator: Main PDF physical pages 4 to 10, Results, Figures and Discussion

paragraphs.text: The authors acknowledge that precise exposure could not be verified with the available equipment. Without unexposed compound-only controls, a compound effect cannot be cleanly separated from an exposure-specific rescue. Handling of donor pairing and repeated observations also needs review. Isolated semen responses and culture concentrations do not establish infertility risk, oral supplement dosing or clinical prevention, and no supplement recommendation follows from this experiment alone.
paragraphs.locator: Main PDF physical pages 2 to 4, Methods; pages 9 to 10, Discussion and limitations

paragraphs.text: The held source is an institutional accepted manuscript examining device-use reports and maternal behavioral screening. Calling, streaming and gaming describe behavior rather than measured absorbed RF dose. Wi-Fi was not carried into the longitudinal models because the categories offered too little contrast. That exclusion should not be presented as a strong prospective demonstration about router exposure or a clinical neurological outcome.
paragraphs.locator: Accepted manuscript physical pages 8 to 9, Methods; pages 23 to 26, Discussion and Conclusion

paragraphs.text: Associations were sporadic and ran in both favorable and unfavorable directions. Some survived false-discovery correction, while other nominal findings did not; neither a uniformly positive nor an entirely null corrected summary is accurate. Self-report, selection, correlated behavior and many comparisons constrain causal interpretation. Numerical reporting remains withheld pending reconciliation, and improved questionnaire categories do not establish an RF benefit or a reason to increase device use.
paragraphs.locator: Accepted manuscript physical pages 18 to 23, main tables, correction footnotes and Discussion; pages 25 to 26, limitations

E02-T03-R264.title: A temperature endpoint under controlled conditions

paragraphs.text: Infrared skin-temperature measurements concern the surface regions observed during a brief controlled session. They do not measure every organ or physiological process. The authors identify the healthy young adult sample and controlled ambient conditions as limits on generalization. Their conclusion about this protocol does not directly validate an exposure-limit threshold or establish what happens during prolonged or repeated exposure.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 10 to 11, limitations and Conclusion

paragraphs.text: A small sample and the measurement interval could miss subtle or rapidly changing temperature responses. Children, older adults and people with altered thermoregulation were not established as covered populations. The unresolved difference between the pooled-result wording and its table also remains material: the source should not be summarized as every analysis being null. Exact numerical interpretation stays withheld while that distinction is unresolved.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 6 to 7, pooled regional result and Table; pages 10 to 11, limitations

E03-T06-R135.title: An instantaneous model needs a time history

paragraphs.text: The model estimates a field at a fixed cooking position. Movement while cooking, heat-output adjustments and time spent at the cooker are separate inputs that the instantaneous estimate does not capture. A useful epidemiological exposure history would need that activity information as well. The model is specific to induction-cooker use, rather than a measurement of every intermediate-frequency source encountered during a day.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 10 to 11, Limitations and Conclusions

paragraphs.text: The household surveys and validation took place in Japan. Applying the model elsewhere requires checking the appliance and voltage conditions, body dimensions and counter geometry. The paper also describes difficulty obtaining appliance specifications from questionnaires. Validation of ordering or prediction within these surveys does not by itself establish an individual absorbed dose, a clinical outcome or one universally superior model.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical page 10, validation discussion and limitations; page 11, Conclusions

E02-T03-R175.title: Recorded calls remain a proxy for dose

paragraphs.text: Operator records improve the measurement of calling behavior, but the baseline observation window does not describe every later call or operating condition. The symptom outcomes were collected by questionnaire at separated times. The authors discuss changes in use, participation and symptom reporting as limitations. A prospective design helps with temporal ordering while retaining those measurement and selection questions.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 9 to 10, Strengths and weaknesses

paragraphs.text: The small headache pattern weakened with confounder adjustment and lacked a clear calling-time gradient. The network-specific pattern also did not align with a straightforward RF-dose explanation, and tinnitus and hearing loss were not associated with baseline call time. Lifestyle or other residual confounding remains possible. These findings do not turn call duration into a causal threshold or make related COSMOS reports independent participants.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 9 to 11, Discussion and Conclusions

E03-T05-R212.title: Read the letter and reply as correspondence

paragraphs.text: The letter challenges exposure geometry, the absence of a sham group and how the transmitting hardware was described. Those are attributed methodological criticisms of the same rat experiment. They are not new animal observations or an independent replication of its fertility findings. The referenced studies in the letter would need their own source-specific checks before being used to extend a health conclusion.
paragraphs.locator: Original one-page letter, printed page 755, complete letter and references

paragraphs.text: In the embedded reply, the investigator describes freely moving animals and changing cage positions, and states that geometry was not measured. The reply also reports consultation about the hardware, without supplying manufacturer correspondence or a measured field map. The exchange therefore leaves dosimetry and control questions open. A published disagreement is not itself a formal correction, proof of misconduct or a new estimate of human fertility risk.
paragraphs.locator: Original one-page letter, printed page 755, Reply of the Author

E06-T11-R208.title: A field survey is not a passenger-outcome study

paragraphs.text: The campaign separates magnetic measurements from band-selective radiofrequency readings during bus operation and charging. Its source-band discussion attributes much of the radiofrequency contribution to surrounding radiocommunication systems. Being measured inside an electric vehicle does not make a signal a battery or motor emission. Route position, nearby base stations and the measurement frequency remain part of the interpretation.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 13 to 17, band-selective results; page 21, Conclusions

paragraphs.text: The report presents environmental readings and distribution fits rather than observed passenger illness, symptoms or implanted-device performance. Local routes and repeated measurements do not establish independent health follow-up. Its suggestions about safety and design therefore extend beyond a measured clinical endpoint. Exact numerical and compliance summaries remain withheld because the existing averaging, condition-label and reference-value questions require clarification.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 21 to 22, Conclusions and study declarations; measurement methods on pages 7 to 10

eeg.title: Analysis choices belong with the EEG finding

paragraphs.text: The sleep report distinguishes all-night recordings from the first sleep episode. Technical problems affected some whole-night recordings, while usable early-episode data were retained. A separate peak-selection issue led to exclusion of a participant from subsequent analysis. An EEG finding therefore belongs with its analysis population and recording interval; it should not be described as if every original recording contributed to every comparison.
paragraphs.locator: Held repository PDF physical pages 6 and 8, EEG methods and spindle analysis

paragraphs.text: The authors describe a genotype-dependent spindle-frequency shift and explicitly state that potential health effects cannot be concluded from it. Their spectral procedure selects the dominant peak and does not separately identify slow and fast spindles at the same channel. That physiological signal and its analysis choices do not establish a neurological diagnosis, a population-wide effect or a clinical sleep-harm threshold.
paragraphs.locator: Held repository PDF physical page 9, Discussion

E02-T03-R248.title: Expectation instructions are the experimental contrast

paragraphs.text: The blinking repeaters were dummy equipment. The assigned difference was what volunteers were told about an enhanced electromagnetic field, together with the warning and laboratory story. This is a test of contextual expectations during perception tasks. It does not compare an actual transmitting router with sham, estimate absorbed RF dose or establish the effects of routine wireless-device use.
paragraphs.locator: Main PDF physical pages 2 to 3, Methods, procedure and cover story

paragraphs.text: The expected group difference in response bias was not demonstrated in either bodily task. Exploratory within-group associations with symptoms remain distinct from that primary comparison, and a positive model in one group with a nonsignificant model in another does not itself establish a group interaction. The student sample, variable credibility of the threat story and task limitations leave clinical and causal interpretation open.
paragraphs.locator: Main PDF physical pages 5 to 7, Results and Discussion

E06-T11-R158.title: Rank agreement is different from identical readings

paragraphs.text: The meters were used simultaneously on selected walking routes, allowing paired comparisons within the bands common to the devices. The distributed meter was calibrated for each assistant, while commercial devices were affected differently by placement and shielding by the body. A similar ranking of environments can coexist with lower absolute readings or weaker agreement in particular bands.
paragraphs.locator: Main PDF physical pages 3 to 6, protocol, Results and Discussion

paragraphs.text: Assistants were instructed not to use their own phones or electronic devices. The campaign therefore characterizes nearby sources under those route conditions rather than the user's own phone dose. Device failures, incomplete common-band coverage and crosstalk also remain relevant. The comparison was not intended to represent average population exposure, and a printed table difference still requires paired-data clarification before numerical reuse.
paragraphs.locator: Main PDF physical pages 3 to 6, measurement restrictions and limitations

E06-T11-R232.title: Spot measurements and extrapolation answer different questions

paragraphs.text: Background readings, streaming and speed tests were taken under different traffic conditions, while the maximum scenario was extrapolated using stated resource and beam assumptions. The phone could switch technology or frequency band, and maximum loading was not always achieved. Those conditions matter when interpreting a comparison with a reference level; an extrapolated value is not an observed lifetime personal dose.
paragraphs.locator: Main PDF physical pages 2 to 3, Methods; page 7, network-control limitations

paragraphs.text: The locations were chosen for access and line of sight near urban and suburban base stations, without a rural sample. This limits population representativeness even when the measured values are below the reference levels used. Distance alone did not reliably predict the field, and the campaign followed no clinical health outcomes. Different distance-fit displays remain numerically unreconciled; neither a universal safe-distance rule nor a disease conclusion is established.
paragraphs.locator: Main PDF physical pages 4 and 7 to 8, distance analysis, Discussion and Conclusions

E02-T03-R062.title: Open and masked sessions need separate interpretation

paragraphs.text: The experiment included known on/off exposures and separate masked comparisons with TETRA-like signals and sham. The open symptom pattern was not reproduced as a consistent exposure-related pattern in the baseline-adjusted masked tests. Those sessions also differed in duration and position in the visit sequence, so the contrast is not a randomized change in knowledge alone.
paragraphs.locator: Main PDF physical pages 2 to 3, Design; pages 5 to 7, Results and Discussion

paragraphs.text: Self-identified sensitive volunteers continued to report more symptoms overall, independently of assigned exposure. The detection and physiological comparisons did not show a consistent signal effect after the stated multiple-comparison treatment. This does not make the reported symptoms unreal. Recruitment shortfalls and brief laboratory observation also prevent conclusions about chronic disease, every possible exposure pattern or formal equivalence between active and sham.
paragraphs.locator: Main PDF physical pages 6 to 7, detection tests, Discussion and limitations

wifi-pmid-33166026.title: Keep the exploratory task result with its limits

paragraphs.text: The word-pair task showed a greater overnight improvement in the Wi-Fi condition, while the emotional and procedural tasks did not show an exposure difference. The authors discuss differences in evening reference performance and uncertainty in the gain estimate. A selected task result should not be expanded into a general memory benefit or a recommendation to seek wireless exposure during sleep.
paragraphs.locator: Held publisher fulltext snapshot, section 3.2 native lines 258 to 261 and section 4.1 lines 406 to 414

paragraphs.text: The analysis was exploratory and did not correct for multiple testing. Exclusions also left exposure sequences unbalanced, and the associated sleep-physiology findings did not corroborate the word-pair result. The authors therefore call the interpretation inconclusive and allow for chance. This memory analysis shares participants with the related sleep report, so the publications do not supply independent replication. The held basis remains a publisher snapshot, without an original PDF or supplement.
paragraphs.locator: Held publisher fulltext snapshot, section 2.7 native lines 243 to 247 and section 4.2 lines 430 to 441

E05-T09-R560.title: Separate exposure surveys from clinical questions

paragraphs.text: The review discusses vehicle field measurements, implant-function experiments, electrocardiographic features and proposed biological pathways. These are different kinds of evidence. A measured field inside a vehicle is not a newly diagnosed passenger condition, and a bench interference result is not a rate of clinical events. The design and endpoint of each original report need to remain attached to any summarized finding.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 2 to 4, Methods and included-study table; pages 6 to 7, device discussion

paragraphs.text: Some included experiments concern broader field exposures rather than direct electric-vehicle use. Applying them to every vehicle, charging system or implant would require additional source-specific justification. The review itself recruits no participants and supplies no pooled patient-risk estimate. Its selection-reporting questions remain unresolved, and proposed mechanisms do not close the causal chain from a particular vehicle exposure to chronic cardiovascular injury.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 2 to 4, eligibility and included studies; pages 6 to 7, mechanisms and interpretation

E05-T09-R232.title: A comet assay does not directly test a disease

paragraphs.text: The experiment assessed cultured Vero cells with comet and cell-cycle methods after a defined pulsed-field exposure. These assays describe selected cellular responses under the laboratory conditions. The discussion proposes an oxidative pathway, but reactive oxygen species were not directly measured in this report. Increased DNA migration therefore does not identify a demonstrated mechanism or establish a human cancer outcome.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 3 to 6, assay methods, Results and Discussion

paragraphs.text: Many evaluated cells are technical observations within a small number of independently repeated experiments. They do not turn that number of experiments into an equally large number of independent exposures. The source also uses inconsistent wording about continuous and intermittent schedules. Without resolving that comparison and the remaining assay controls, neither a precise schedule ranking nor a real-world household or workplace risk estimate should be inferred.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 3 to 4, treatment and statistical methods; pages 4 to 6, schedule interpretation

E05-T10-R110.title: Static-magnet interaction is a device-specific question

paragraphs.text: The laboratory tests deliberately searched for relative positions where the phone magnet could activate a generator's magnetic mode. The response varied with position and stopped when the phone was removed. This identifies a localized static-magnet interaction in the tested devices. It is different from a radiofrequency dose study or an observation that phone use caused a general cardiovascular disease.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 2 to 4, objective and Methods; page 6, Results and Discussion

paragraphs.text: No implanted patients were tested. Body anatomy, implant placement, actual use patterns and later product designs remain separate questions. The manufacturers supplied devices and programming assistance, as the acknowledgements disclose. The bench findings cannot quantify how often a clinically important event occurs in everyday use, establish compatibility for every product or provide a universal spacing rule. Model-specific clinical advice is outside this experiment.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 6 to 7, laboratory versus in-vivo interpretation, Conclusions and acknowledgements

glossary-index.title: Use definitions with the source design

paragraphs.text: A measurement term does not make different instruments interchangeable. The body-worn-meter comparison shows how similar ranking of environments can coexist with different absolute readings because bands, calibration and shielding by the body differ. When using definitions for field strength or exposure assessment, keep the instrument and measurement setting with the result rather than treating every reading as an individual absorbed dose.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 4 to 6, instrument comparison Discussion and limitations

paragraphs.text: Time and position also belong with an exposure term. The induction-cooker model estimates an instantaneous field at a fixed position, while movement, heat-output changes and cooking duration need additional information. A glossary definition helps name the quantity, but does not supply the missing activity history or turn that model into a measured clinical risk.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 10 to 11, Limitations and Conclusions

paragraphs.text: An outcome term needs the same care. In the sleep study, a genotype-dependent EEG spindle-frequency finding was not a conclusion about potential health effects. Reading the recording method and analysis population alongside the term helps distinguish a physiological endpoint from a diagnosis, a population-wide effect or a clinical sleep-harm claim. The underlying scientific appraisal and human review remain pending.
paragraphs.locator: Held repository PDF physical page 9, Discussion

paragraphs.text: Participants knew whether the experimental RF signal was on or off. That open comparison combines actual exposure with information about exposure, unlike a masked RF-versus-sham test. The symptom difference cannot therefore isolate a biological RF mechanism from expectation or the laboratory context. The sample also consisted mainly of healthy young volunteers rather than a clinical group with established long-term illness.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 15 to 16, Discussion and open-label limitations

paragraphs.text: The alarmist video increased perceived risk without producing a significant video effect on the symptom or cortisol outcomes. Cortisol also did not track the reported symptom change. The authors discuss timing, anticipatory stress and limited sensitivity to small effects as possible limitations. A null comparison under this protocol is not an equivalence test or proof that every expectation or stress response is absent.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 13 to 16, Results and Discussion

E02-T03-R242.title: Individual sessions do not become independent people

paragraphs.text: The protocol was individualized with participant input, using mixed sources and real-versus-sham sessions. Repeated sessions provide information about a participant within that protocol, but do not supply an equal number of independent participants. Selection, tolerance of testing and differences in personal schedules constrain how far the collective result can be generalized to everyone reporting environmental intolerance.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 4 to 5, co-design, source conditions and masking; pages 6 to 8, participants; pages 16 to 17, limitations

paragraphs.text: The nominal individual detection exception did not survive removal of the least-certain session. Associations between perceived exposure and symptom reporting also remain joint self-reports, rather than a randomized manipulation of belief alone. They do not prove that symptoms are unreal or establish a clinical nocebo explanation for every participant. The results require the stated repeated-session and multiple-comparison context.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 15 to 17, individual interpretation and limitations

E05-T09-R451.title: The donor pool is not an individual susceptibility test

paragraphs.text: The experiment pooled blood-cell material within demographic groups before laboratory exposure. A response in an older-group pool cannot identify how each donor responded or separate age from every other group difference. Culture and serum conditions also matter. The reported high-condition comet finding should remain an assay-specific result, not an individual cancer prediction or a clinical classification of older phone users.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 2 to 5, donors, Methods and Results; page 9, Discussion

paragraphs.text: The combined-treatment experiments generally did not show enhanced chemically induced damage under the tested sequences. Selected decreases do not establish protection in exposed workers or a treatment benefit. There were few independently repeated exposures, while many cells and slides provided technical measurements. Those are different units of information; uncertainty in donor variation and replicate handling is not resolved by counting more scored cells.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 3 to 4, experimental and statistical methods; pages 8 to 9, combined treatments and Discussion

E02-T03-R229.title: Physiological observations are not cognition or injury

paragraphs.text: The study measured regional skin temperature and electrodermal responses during a brief controlled laboratory protocol. Selected metrics changed, while other metrics did not. The authors discuss possible cognitive interpretations, but cognitive performance was not itself the measured endpoint. These recordings do not establish improved decision-making, clinical benefit or tissue injury. A physiological difference and a health consequence remain separate questions.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 6 to 11, Results, Figures and Discussion

paragraphs.text: Interpretation remains restricted to the tested signal, exposure geometry and selected healthy volunteers. The paper calls for replication and acknowledges uncontrolled variables. Repeated recordings and related metrics are not independent participants. Because directional and labeling questions remain unresolved, neither a numerical effect summary nor a single direction for all skin-conductance results is released here. No long-term disease inference follows from this short protocol.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 10 to 11, Discussion and Conclusion

E05-T09-R485.title: A controlled null remains specific to its apparatus

paragraphs.text: The refined setup monitored RF power and controlled temperature while measuring selected cell-growth and stress-related endpoints. The thermally controlled comparisons did not show a significant RF-related pattern in those assays. This is evidence about the tested cell models, signal and observation period, rather than a measurement of cancer incidence or the response of an intact person during ordinary device use.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 6 to 8, Results; page 11, Conclusion

paragraphs.text: Switching off cooling increased temperature together with growth-related measurements. That comparison makes thermal control relevant to interpretation, but does not independently establish the cause of every earlier study result. Limited independent experiments, differing replicate wording and absence of a formal equivalence margin constrain the null findings. The source cannot exclude every subtle, long-term or tissue-specific effect or establish universal human safety.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 8 to 11, cooling-disabled comparison and Discussion

E01-T01-R251.title: Keep self-reported behavior separate from absorbed dose

paragraphs.text: The investigators compared women with confirmed breast cancer, women referred for mammography and controls without breast abnormalities. The suspected group was exploratory and was not a second group with confirmed cancer. Calling, screen time and phone placement came from interviews. These measures describe reported behavior rather than directly measured breast radiofrequency dose, and the retrospective comparison does not establish which aspect of phone use explains an association.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical page 3, study groups, data collection and exposure definitions

paragraphs.text: The printed case and control totals do not agree consistently with the Methods, and the screen-time reference category in the regression table does not support a simple reading of generic prose about longer use. These reporting issues remain unresolved. The source itself acknowledges self-report and residual confounding. Its findings should not become a numerical risk estimate, a causal breast-cancer claim or a prevention recommendation while those source-specific problems and scientific review remain open.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical page 3, Methods; page 6, Table 2; page 8, Table 4 reference footnote; page 9, conclusions

E02-T03-R018.title: Separate randomized exposure from perceived exposure

paragraphs.text: Computer-controlled exposure supported a randomized, double-blind crossover comparison of acute base-station-like signals. The well-being questionnaires did not show a significant exposure-response association in either participant group. Cognitive findings depended on the task and group, and the nominal findings did not remain significant after the reported adjustment across cognitive endpoints. A selected unadjusted result should therefore remain attached to its analysis rather than being described as a consistent cognitive impairment.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical page 2, design; page 4, questionnaire and cognitive Results with multiple-endpoint adjustment

paragraphs.text: Perceived field strength was associated with poorer reported well-being independently of actual exposure condition, while the perception ratings did not track the randomized field as a group. That distinction is useful, but an observational association between perception and symptoms does not establish an individual symptom cause or prove a clinical nocebo mechanism. The authors also emphasize the short exposure duration. The experiment cannot establish long-term safety, clinical equivalence or the absence of every possible brain response.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 4 to 5, perception Results and Discussion; page 6, exposure-duration limitation

E01-T01-R257.title: Keep the tumour analysis with survival and reporting limits

paragraphs.text: The Japanese report describes an animal arm of a coordinated programme, with tumour follow-up and parallel genotoxicity experiments. Its survival-adjusted tumour analysis did not find a significant increase, while some unadjusted comparisons differed from that result. Survival differed among groups and apparatus-related losses affected the analysis. These details matter when interpreting rare events: a nonsignificant survival-adjusted result is not a precise estimate of human cancer risk or proof that all exposure conditions are equivalent.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 7 to 8, survival, neoplastic findings and analysis-dependent comparisons

paragraphs.text: The main tumour table and Results describe an exposed-group cardiac schwannoma, whereas the Discussion says that there were no exposed cases. That contradiction remains visible and unresolved. The selected source passages do not justify silently choosing the zero-case wording or repairing the report from surrounding interpretation. The coordinated companion design also should not be counted as independent design replication. Formal scientific appraisal, numerical release and human review remain pending.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical page 3, Table 2; page 7, cardiac findings; page 12, conflicting Discussion statement

E05-T09-R078.title: Read the final analysis rather than preliminary gene lists

paragraphs.text: The laboratory study examined lymphocyte DNA endpoints and gene-expression patterns in lymphocytes and yeast. Its final analyses did not retain an exposure-related expression change, and the authors reported no exposure-related DNA alteration under the tested conditions. That is a result for selected assays, models and exposure arrangements. It does not establish that every cellular pathway is unchanged or provide a direct measure of disease risk in people.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 5 to 9, Results and concluding Discussion

paragraphs.text: Human gene-expression measurements used pooled donor RNA, and different donors contributed at different field intensities. The authors state that this prevented their planned dose-response approach for those data. Duplicate arrays describe technical measurement, not independent replication in separate people. Culture conditions and temperature also affected ancillary assay observations discussed in the paper. Preliminary nominal gene lists, pooled final analyses and clinical evidence must remain separate rather than being combined into a broad health conclusion.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 4 to 5, RNA pooling and analysis; page 9, Discussion of culture conditions and interpretation

E05-T09-R513.title: The tested cell responses are narrower than a skin-health claim

paragraphs.text: The experiment assigned exposure conditions across chambers using a blind protocol and monitored sample temperature, including compensation for exposure-related heating. It measured redox-sensor responses and repair of ultraviolet-induced DNA lesions in established cell models. The authors reported no significant exposed-versus-sham differences for the selected responses under those controlled conditions. An assay-specific null result is not a clinical trial of intact skin and does not by itself establish equivalence across all possible responses.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical page 4, exposure control; pages 8 to 11, redox and DNA-repair results and interpretation

paragraphs.text: The ultraviolet challenge and measured DNA photoproducts should stay attached to the repair result. They are not interchangeable with every DNA-damage assay or with spontaneous disease in people. The authors explicitly note that the acute in-vitro protocols do not reproduce chronic real-life exposure. Established altered cell models, the specified challenges and remaining supplementary-reporting questions constrain transfer. Neither universal human safety nor a clinical protective effect follows from the controlled cellular observations.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 8 to 11, ultraviolet challenge, CPD repair, model comparisons and duration limitation

E06-T12-R016.title: Reduced bench interference is not demonstrated patient benefit

paragraphs.text: The artificial chest arrangement combined pacemakers, leads, swine tissue and saline to test transient-field interference. Twisting the excess leads reduced induced voltage and aggregate pacing inhibition relative to the parallel arrangement in the tested systems. The aggregate figure still includes inhibition in the tested conditions. A favorable example trace therefore does not establish elimination of interference, and repeated electrical pulses are not independent patients or observations of everyday clinical event frequency.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 2 to 3, simulation setup; pages 7 to 8, Figures 5 and 6 with aggregate inhibition

paragraphs.text: The authors identify the non-beating tissue model, near-source geometry and selected dual-chamber devices as limits, and describe possible lead-dislocation, abrasion and extraction drawbacks. Their brief clinical anecdote does not supply a controlled comparison or a clear patient denominator. The experiment should not become an implantation recommendation or a general compatibility rule. Ambiguous statistical annotations and the held supplement inconsistency remain unresolved; scientific and human review are still pending.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical page 9, clinical anecdote and limitations; pages 7 to 8, comparison annotations; held supplement Table_1.docx, native Table I

E03-T05-R222.title: A motility-category shift is not a fertility outcome

paragraphs.text: The mouse experiment measured later sperm and tissue indicators rather than mating success. Its reported motility change involved more non-progressive movement and fewer immotile sperm, without a significant change in progressive movement. Sperm counts, head abnormalities and reproductive tissue weights did not show significant exposure-related differences. These endpoints should stay distinct: an altered movement category is not demonstrated improvement in fertilization, a fertility treatment or a direct estimate of human reproductive risk.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 4 to 5, Results, Figure 5 and Discussion of fertility indicators

paragraphs.text: Technical failures affected the exposure cohorts and the motility analysis, including exclusion of an early cohort from the motility results. Sampling also occurred after an unexposed interval, so it does not describe an immediate response during exposure. These timing and missingness details qualify the comparison and its precision. Many scored sperm cells remain observations within animals, rather than independent exposed animals. The apparatus, exposure schedule and selected later indicators limit transfer to chronic human fertility questions.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical page 3, design and exposure cohorts; pages 4 to 5, motility technical loss and sampling description

E02-T04-R161.title: Operator records improve a proxy without measuring every sleep exposure

paragraphs.text: The prospective COSMOS analysis linked baseline operator-recorded calling with later questionnaire sleep outcomes. Network information allowed a separate weighting intended to reflect different radiofrequency output between networks. Most sleep outcomes showed no consistent adverse pattern, while an insomnia association at high ordinary call time weakened with the network-related weighting. This supports keeping ordinary calling behavior separate from the RF proxy rather than attributing the association directly to absorbed dose.
paragraphs.locator: Held native PMC fulltext XML, Methods section 2.2; Results and Discussion on network-weighted call time

paragraphs.text: The sleep outcome was questionnaire-derived, and the insomnia indicator did not include the duration and frequency requirements of a complete clinical diagnosis. Exposure records covered baseline calling, without a continuous history of phone behavior, sleep outcomes or stress throughout follow-up; network type came from the first base station of a call. Screen use, nighttime interruptions and other unmeasured behaviors remain separate explanations. A misfiled archive PDF remains quarantined; these notes use the exact-identity native XML and do not upgrade that source basis.
paragraphs.locator: Held native PMC fulltext XML, Methods sections 2.2 to 2.3; Strength and limitations; exact source-basis record

E03-T05-R176.title: An isolated-sample signal does not measure a couple’s fertility

paragraphs.text: The same ejaculated semen sample supplied exposed and unexposed portions, which reduces differences between donors in the comparison. The authors reported endpoint-dependent changes: fragmentation and clusterin signals increased, while motility and acrosin decreases were significant in the abnormal-semen groups but not in the normozoospermic group. The abstract’s broad wording should be read with that Results distinction. These are immediate laboratory measurements, without measured conception, pregnancy or live birth.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical page 2, paired design; page 4, Results and Table 1; page 5, molecular figures

paragraphs.text: The commercial handset specification is not a measurement of absorbed dose in the semen. Sample-specific dosimetry, a measured temperature history and clear assay masking were not supplied, and simultaneous clusterin and fragmentation changes do not demonstrate mediation by oxidative stress. The authors acknowledge that repeated exposure and reversibility were not tested. The report therefore cannot quantify pocket-carriage infertility, permanent injury or a clinical risk for phone users, and scientific review remains pending.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 2 to 4, exposure, assays and statistical methods; pages 6 to 7, interpretation and limitations

E06-T11-R227.title: Keep the phone activity with the meter reading

paragraphs.text: The campaign compared selected microenvironments with an inactive test phone and with deliberately intensive download or upload activity. Active tasks increased external RF readings, and the urban-rural comparison depended on the scenario. These observations describe the instrument, route and test-phone arrangement. They are not independently followed patients, lifetime population doses or clinical outcomes, and repeated time samples within routes should not be counted as independent studies.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 2 to 4, routes, scenarios, measurement and analysis; pages 7 to 9, scenario interpretation

paragraphs.text: The shared time-division band could not distinguish signals from the nearby phone and the base station. A higher reading during download cannot therefore be assigned entirely to base-station beamforming or converted directly into absorbed organ dose. Body shielding, operator and device differences, missing active scenarios and unavailable supplements constrain interpretation. Country-level differences cannot isolate the effect of regulation from network and sampling differences, and this exposure survey does not establish a health-policy benefit or harm.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 3 to 4, setup and failed scenarios; pages 8 to 9, signal attribution, strengths and limitations

E04-T07-R257.title: Apartment position is a proxy, not a child’s measured dose

paragraphs.text: TransExpo used registry and building information to compare children whose apartments occupied different positions relative to built-in transformer rooms. Exposure classification was blinded to case or control status. Pilot measurements helped justify the apartment categories, but were not measurements in the included children’s homes. The design reduces the need for active household participation while retaining uncertainty about each child’s actual exposure and residential history. It remains an observational comparison rather than randomized exposure.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 2 to 3, study design, pilot exposure classification and blinding

paragraphs.text: The planned matched analysis did not show a clear association, while alternative models produced weak elevations. The paper explains that the conditional model dropped some matched sets and that highly exposed cases were sparse. These model-specific findings should not be collapsed into either a precise risk increase or proof of no possible association. Wide uncertainty and exposure-category overlap limit conclusions, and pilot exposure studies are not independent confirmations of the childhood-leukaemia result.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical page 5, pooled analyses and Table 5; page 6, Discussion and limitations

E06-T11-R114.title: Average and peak readings answer different measurement questions

paragraphs.text: In the classroom walkthrough, active Wi-Fi produced a higher sampled average than idle Wi-Fi, without a statistically significant difference in the sampled maximum. The authors relate this to more frequent transmission rather than a higher transmitted peak. A short-window average and a short-window maximum should therefore remain separately labelled. Neither quantity is a child’s measured full-day absorbed dose or a direct observation of sleep, learning or disease.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical page 4, walkthrough Results and Figure 1; page 7, active-versus-idle interpretation

paragraphs.text: Most classrooms were empty during measurement, and the occupied-room comparison was a small part of the survey. It does not establish that every class size, traffic pattern or device configuration produces the same exposure. Source rankings also changed between indoor and schoolyard settings and between average and peak measures. The measured environmental fields and the comparison with cited reference levels should not become a clinical-harm finding or a universal claim about all school networks.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical page 2, classroom recruitment and measurement setting; pages 4 to 7, source comparisons and occupied-room limitations

E03-T06-R096.title: A dependency score is not fetal radiofrequency dosimetry

paragraphs.text: The Kumamoto adjunct classified excessive use with a text-message dependency subscale. Its comparator was ordinary use, rather than a group with no phone use. This makes the exposure measure behavioral: it does not isolate transmitted radiofrequency energy, absorbed fetal dose or a particular phone model. The lower average birth weight reported in the excessive-use group also needs to remain distinct from the categorical low-birth-weight comparison, which was not statistically significant.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical page 2, dependency scale and group definitions; page 5, Table 2; page 6, Results interpretation

paragraphs.text: The emergency-transport association came from sparse events, and the authors explicitly allow for chance. They also state that mental-health factors were not accounted for, although such factors could relate both to dependent phone behavior and pregnancy outcomes. The report does not provide transport indications or severity sufficient to turn that association into a specific neonatal diagnosis. These observational findings do not demonstrate an RF mechanism or establish a phone-use safety threshold during pregnancy.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 3 and 5, outcome Results and Table 2; page 6, limitations and mental-health discussion

E04-T07-R237.title: Parental job averages are a different exposure question

paragraphs.text: The CLIC pooling linked parental occupational titles to a job-exposure matrix for workplace magnetic fields. Paternal and maternal periods of interest were defined separately. These job-average estimates are not measurements of a child’s residential field or absorbed dose, and people with the same job title may have different tasks and exposure histories. Harmonizing job codes across contributing studies improves comparability but does not remove the proxy nature of the exposure.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 2 to 3, occupational exposure matrix, periods and harmonization

paragraphs.text: The harmonized individual-data analyses did not show a clear association with the childhood-leukaemia outcomes. The expanded literature analysis gave a different, borderline paternal result and raised publication-bias concerns. These are not interchangeable analyses or independent replications to be simply added together. Missing parental job histories and differential maternal missingness were identified as selection concerns. The paper’s null and borderline findings therefore retain their specific datasets, exposure definitions and uncertainty rather than establishing a universal occupational-risk conclusion.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical page 4, pooled and expanded analyses; page 7, exposure misclassification and missing-history limitations

E02-T04-R122.title: The nested sleep measurements belong to the same cohort

paragraphs.text: QUALIFEX used several exposure surrogates, including reported phone use, modeled environmental fields and bedroom or personal measurements. The linked actigraphy and diary study sampled a subset of the cohort, so it is not independent replication of the questionnaire analysis. Actigraphy describes movement-based sleep duration and efficiency rather than EEG sleep architecture. Its reported category comparisons did not show significant associations with those sleep measures, without establishing clinical equivalence for every possible sleep endpoint.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 2 to 4, nested recruitment and exposure methods; page 5, Table 3; page 7, actigraphy rationale

paragraphs.text: The longitudinal analyses included nominally significant contrasts but no consistent adverse exposure-response pattern. The authors did not apply a formal correction across endpoints, instead considering consistency and biological plausibility. That is different from every statistical test being null. Modeled ambient fields, nearby handset use and bedroom measurements also capture different parts of exposure. They cannot be treated as a continuous record of absorbed dose or used to rule out all responses in people who report particular sensitivities.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical page 4, questionnaire Results; page 7, interpretation and multiple-endpoint approach; pages 7 to 8, exposure limits

E03-T05-R267.title: Sperm biomarkers and selected fertilization assays stay distinct

paragraphs.text: The mouse study reported mature-sperm vitality, motility and oxidative or DNA-marker changes, with responses differing across tissues, assays and exposure periods. The mitochondrial probe signal did not follow the same pattern as the general oxidative probe, and its time pattern was not uniform. These observations support the authors’ oxidative interpretation while leaving the precise initiating RF interaction unresolved. They do not supply a human infertility rate or show that every tissue and endpoint responds in the same way.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 2 to 4, Results and oxidative probes; page 7, duration-dependent interpretation

paragraphs.text: The selected fertilization and early embryo assays did not show significant impairment under the tested conditions. The authors acknowledge that their in-vitro fertilization strategy selected higher-quality motile sperm, which limits the comparison with the broader recovered sperm population. Those early assays did not measure natural mating success, live birth or later offspring health. Neither the biomarker findings nor the selected functional nulls justify treating all reproductive outcomes as equivalent or translating the mouse regimen directly to ordinary phone carriage.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical page 4, fertilization Results; pages 7 to 8, sperm selection and unmeasured later outcomes

E02-T04-R143.title: A birth-cohort setting does not make every comparison prospective

paragraphs.text: The child-sleep analysis was nested within a birth cohort, but parents recalled earlier phone use in the same survey that collected current sleep reports. The authors note that this part of the analysis resembles a cross-sectional comparison and may be affected by reporting bias. Household Wi-Fi or cordless-phone presence was another exposure proxy, not a measurement of nighttime absorbed dose. The design did not test whether switching off a router improves a child’s sleep.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 3 to 4, recalled phone use, household-source questions and sleep assessment; pages 11 to 12, reporting and design limitations

paragraphs.text: The researchers prespecified some sleep subscales as possible negative controls for unmeasured confounding. Higher mobile calling was associated with less favorable scores in several domains, but findings differed across mobile, cordless and modeled environmental-source comparisons. That mixed pattern does not isolate a radiofrequency cause. The questionnaire sleep-duration score also differs from calculated hours in bed. Keeping source type, outcome definition and common reporting method attached to each result prevents a general clinical sleep-harm conclusion.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 4 to 6, outcome definitions and negative-control analysis; pages 11 to 12, mixed-source interpretation

E06-T11-R137.title: Transmission timing and the tested device mode matter

paragraphs.text: The residential-device work measured peak fields and transmission timing, then used duty cycle and placement in its exposure comparisons. Infrequent smart-meter transmission can make a time-averaged quantity differ substantially from a peak reading. This is an exposure-characterization exercise, not a study of diagnosed illness or development. A device measured at a particular distance and operating state should not be described as a direct measurement of an individual organ’s absorbed dose.
paragraphs.locator: Held final-manuscript PDF physical pages 5 to 8, measurement methods; pages 18 to 21, duty-cycle interpretation and exposure limits

paragraphs.text: The Bluetooth measurements involved a computer mouse and speakers during failed pairing attempts. They did not characterize earbuds worn at the head or every Bluetooth mode. The manuscript also cautions that its household placements form a small cross-section in space and time that cannot be generalized to all smart homes. These mode and sampling limits belong with the reported readings. Source identity is preserved as the held final manuscript, without claiming access to a publisher-typeset version.
paragraphs.locator: Held final-manuscript PDF physical page 17, Bluetooth device mode; page 21, sampling and generalization limits; pages 33 to 34, Table 5

E03-T06-R094.title: Favorable developmental associations do not establish an RF benefit

paragraphs.text: MoBa linked reported maternal phone talking during pregnancy with later parent-reported language, communication and motor screens. Some associations were favorable, but reported talking was not measured fetal RF dose. Parental phone use also tracked social and personal characteristics. The presence of paternal associations in a similar direction supports considering shared family or social factors rather than treating a maternal association as evidence that radiofrequency exposure improved fetal development.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 2 to 4, exposure, outcomes and covariates; page 9, paternal findings and confounding interpretation

paragraphs.text: The outcomes were developmental screening measures rather than a complete diagnostic assessment. Children not yet talking were excluded from the sentence-complexity analysis, and motor instruments differed between follow-ups. These details limit claims about all children or all developmental conditions. Remaining exposure and outcome misclassification and unmeasured confounding also constrain interpretation. The findings should not become a recommendation to increase phone use during pregnancy or a precise estimate of a fetal radiofrequency effect.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 2 to 3, sentence-complexity exclusion and screening instruments; page 9, misclassification and observational limitations

E04-T08-R044.title: Read the baseline analysis beneath the prospective study title

paragraphs.text: The ExPOSURE study-design section explicitly identifies this paper as baseline cross-sectional results within a prospective cohort. It therefore compares reported phone use with cognition at that assessment, rather than measuring within-child cognitive change caused by later exposure. Parents and children gave different reports of phone ownership or use, adding uncertainty to the behavioral exposure proxy. The disagreement does not identify which individual report was correct or provide an objective measure of brain RF dose.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 2 to 3, study design and exposure questions; page 6, parent-child reporting discrepancy

paragraphs.text: Most baseline cognitive comparisons were not significant, alongside selected differences in response speed or accuracy. The analyses did not adjust for multiple comparisons, and the authors treated possible gender differences as exploratory. They sought consistent patterns rather than relying on an isolated significant result. These laboratory task measures are not developmental diagnoses or proof that phone use caused cognitive impairment. A prospective cohort label does not remove the baseline comparison’s confounding, reporting uncertainty or chance explanations.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 3 to 4, analysis strategy; pages 6 to 9, cognitive results, interpretation and exploratory conclusion

E02-T04-R174.title: Different sleep comparisons within the same report

paragraphs.text: The usual-use and evening analyses did not use interchangeable exposure histories. The all-day model relied on questionnaires, whereas the repeated evening comparison used children’s diaries alongside wrist recordings in a smaller cohort subset. The evening phone-call category combined mobile and cordless calls. Its shorter-sleep association therefore belongs to that defined comparison, rather than to every screen activity or to a direct experiment switching a router on and off.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 2 to 4, Methods 2.1 to 2.4; page 7, Table 6 and footnote a

paragraphs.text: The exposure model combined reported activity with assumed network use, output power and device positions. These estimates were not measurements of each child’s absorbed brain dose. The discussion also states that estimated evening call dose and calling duration were strongly correlated, preventing the authors from separating RF exposure from the circumstances of calling. Mental arousal and displaced sleep remain possible explanations, without either being demonstrated as the cause by this analysis.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical page 3, integrated exposure model and assumptions; page 8, Discussion 4.2 and 4.5

E03-T05-R182.title: Separate reproductive endpoints from a fertility conclusion

paragraphs.text: The experiment assessed sperm samples, reproductive tissues and cell-death markers after exposure of male rats. Those endpoints are related but did not all follow the same daily-duration pattern: the longer-duration group showed the clearer tissue and apoptosis findings, while some sperm measurements were more changed in the shorter-duration group. A general claim that every reproductive measure steadily worsened with longer daily exposure would lose that endpoint-specific pattern. Mating success and human conception were not measured.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 2 to 4, animal exposure and endpoint methods; pages 5 to 6, Results, Tables 2 to 3 and Figures 2 to 4

paragraphs.text: The methods describe the antenna arrangement and exposure schedules but do not provide a quantified delivered field or absorbed dose for this experiment. Its discussion cites exposure quantities from other experiments; those values cannot fill the gap in this setup. The proposed hormonal and oxidative explanations likewise exceed the measurements made here: the assays concern sperm, tissue structure and apoptosis, without direct testosterone or reactive-oxygen-species measurements establishing those proposed pathways.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical page 2, Exposure system; pages 3 to 4, endpoint assays; pages 7 to 8, Discussion and comparisons with other studies

E02-T03-R227.title: Read the device and the available recordings together

paragraphs.text: The active and sham units were modified baby monitors used in healthy adults’ bedrooms. The report identifies the signal modulation as well as its frequency band, and cautions that transferring the results to devices using different modulations is difficult. This is an adult sleep experiment with a particular transmitting system. A shared frequency band does not turn it into a direct trial of every Wi-Fi router, an infant-development study or a measurement of each participant’s whole-night absorbed dose.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 2 to 3, device and study procedure; pages 8 to 9, Strengths and limitations

paragraphs.text: Subjective sleep scores, EEG bands, actigraphy and heart-rate measures did not supply one uniform result. The paper reports selected subjective and EEG differences alongside nonsignificant comparisons for other measures. Attrition, incomplete recordings and technical problems left different available samples and unequal order groups. The authors acknowledge multiple analyses and possible chance findings. Those limits matter when interpreting the reported differences; a nonsignificant comparison in this small pilot also does not establish equivalence or universal absence of an effect.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical page 5, Results and Statistical analysis; pages 6 to 7, Table 1 and Figure 2; pages 8 to 9, limitations

t33.title: A research phone app is not the field sensor

paragraphs.text: The European measurement survey used phone software to run download and upload scenarios and record network information. RF fields were measured by a separate frequency-selective exposimeter carried with the phone. A diary application recorded timing and location, then its records were merged with the instrument data. The presence of an app in that workflow therefore does not show that an ordinary phone application alone measured the surrounding RF field.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical page 3, Methods 2.2 to 2.4, mobile phone scenarios, measurement device and measurement setup

paragraphs.text: The survey also corrected cross-talk between nearby measurement bands and identified limits in distinguishing uplink from downlink in a shared time-division band. These are instrument and signal-classification issues, separate from a phone’s display of its connection state. The study describes external fields under selected activity scenarios, without deriving an individual organ dose or measuring health outcomes. It cannot validate an unrelated detector app or convert that app’s display into a clinical conclusion.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 3 to 4, Methods 2.5.1 cross-talk corrections; page 9, Strengths and limitations

t23.title: Read oven protection and injury reports by their purpose

paragraphs.text: The FDA describes oven interlocks that stop microwave production when the door is opened, along with a monitoring system for interlock failure. Its discussion places leakage limits within a product-performance standard and laboratory testing programme. That is a defined assessment of microwave ovens. A change in a nearby wireless connection does not reproduce the standard’s leakage measurement or inspect whether a particular oven’s door and protective systems are functioning correctly.
paragraphs.locator: Held FDA HTML, Microwave Oven Safety Standard, interlock systems and FDA testing paragraphs

paragraphs.text: The same page distinguishes unusual radiation-injury circumstances from the much more common burns involving hot containers, food or liquids. Its account of superheated water concerns an eruption of hot liquid after disturbance, not food becoming radioactive. Keeping the injury mechanism explicit prevents a report of a cooking burn from being treated as a leakage measurement. The FDA source provides product and use context, without supplying a diagnosis for an individual incident.
paragraphs.locator: Held FDA HTML, Cooking with Microwaves; Avoiding Injuries from Super-Heated Water in Microwave Ovens; Have Radiation Injuries Resulted from Microwave Ovens?

t22.title: Measure bursts as well as the spaces between them

paragraphs.text: The residential-device report determined transmission frequencies, peak fields and duty cycles separately. For smart meters, a prominent transmission peak could coexist with a small time-averaged contribution because transmissions were infrequent and the device was positioned away from residents. The result depends on those operating and placement conditions. A peak reading alone is therefore an incomplete description of the tested meter’s exposure pattern, rather than a value that necessarily persists throughout the day.
paragraphs.locator: Held final-manuscript PDF physical pages 4 to 7, objective and measurement method; pages 18 to 19, Discussion A

paragraphs.text: The authors found that their handheld broadband setup could miss short or weak signals and could not distinguish sources, so they omitted its results from the reported device characterisation. Their frequency-selective method addressed a different measurement task. They also caution that the selected homes and source placements form a cross-section in space and time, without generalisation to all smart homes. Neither that survey nor its equipment comparison tested a health benefit from a meter shield.
paragraphs.locator: Held final-manuscript PDF physical pages 20 to 21, Strengths and Limitations; pages 4 to 7, study scope and instrumentation

t12.title: Keep cookware and the assessment quantity visible

paragraphs.text: FOPH explains that the pan receives energy through induced currents and magnetisation, while some magnetic field remains outside the pan. Its operating recommendations distinguish suitable cookware, pan size, centring and cooker settings. These details describe the coupled cooker-and-pan system. A measurement made with one pan arrangement cannot establish the exposure for every other arrangement merely because the hob has the same name or nominal power setting.
paragraphs.locator: Held FOPH PDF physical pages 1 to 2, induction explanation and operating recommendations

paragraphs.text: The fact sheet separates comparison with magnetic-field limits from the available studies of pregnancy outcomes. It explains that the limit includes a safety margin, so a field result relative to that limit is not itself an observed health outcome. The document also treats electronic implants as a distinct compatibility concern. These distinctions prevent a general cooker exposure comparison from being presented as either a pregnancy-risk estimate or a functional test of someone’s implanted device.
paragraphs.locator: Held FOPH PDF physical page 1, field limits and pregnancy literature; pages 1 to 2, electronic-implant recommendation

t06.title: Define what a protective accessory is claimed to change

paragraphs.text: FOPH’s mobile-phone fact sheet warns that shielding, harmonising or neutralising products can impair the phone’s network connection and thereby increase its radiation. This concerns how the phone operates: it may respond to the changed connection. It is not a controlled clinical trial demonstrating an illness benefit or harm for every sticker or pendant. An accessory claim therefore needs evidence for its actual use configuration, rather than a conclusion transferred from a marketing label.
paragraphs.locator: Held FOPH PDF physical pages 1 to 2, connection-quality explanation and protective/shielding/harmonising-product paragraph

paragraphs.text: ICNIRP distinguishes external reference levels from basic restrictions expressed in absorbed quantities. That distinction is relevant when a product demonstration shows only a local field-meter display. A reading outside the body and a claim about absorbed exposure are different endpoints, and neither alone is a clinical outcome. The guidance supplies a framework for those quantities; it does not provide a matched efficacy trial of the stickers, pendants or harmonisers discussed in this question.
paragraphs.locator: Held ICNIRP RF HTML, Protection, basic-restriction and external-reference-level paragraphs

t40.title: Separate a field assessment from a magnet-mode experiment

paragraphs.text: ICNIRP’s low-frequency explanation distinguishes the external electric and magnetic fields from electric fields induced inside the body. Its basic restrictions and external reference levels therefore describe different quantities linked through exposure assumptions. That framework can help identify what a technical report needs to assess, but this context page is not a measurement of a particular phone charging pad. A charger-specific conclusion still needs the actual equipment, field regime and operating arrangement.
paragraphs.locator: Held ICNIRP LF HTML, Frequency range and LF use; Protection

paragraphs.text: The MagSafe experiment tested magnetic-mode activation in demo pacemaker and defibrillator generators while varying the phone’s position. The investigators also tested case and wallet configurations and mapped the phone’s static magnetic field. Those observations concern the magnets and the tested implanted-device functions, rather than an experiment measuring inductive charging dose or charging-related illness. Retaining the tested endpoint prevents this bench result from becoming a universal rule about the exposure of all wireless chargers.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 2 to 4, Methods 2.1 to 2.3 and Results 3.1; page 6, Discussion

t13.title: The tested implanted system is part of the evidence

paragraphs.text: The transient-field experiment placed pacemakers and leads in a swine-tissue chest model immersed in saline. It compared excess-lead arrangements while measuring induced voltages and pacing inhibition. This made the lead geometry part of the tested system, rather than an incidental detail. This model did not follow implanted patients or reproduce a beating heart, so its engineering comparison cannot supply a patient event rate or an instruction to change an implanted lead arrangement.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 2 to 4, Simulation Model, Figure 1 and Study Protocol; pages 6 to 9, Results and Discussion limits, including the non-beating-heart limitation on page 9

paragraphs.text: The MagSafe bench study activated magnetic mode only at particular relative positions of the phone and generators, with normal mode returning after phone removal. It did not involve implanted patients. The paper discusses body anatomy and implant placement as reasons that in-vivo work would answer additional questions. A local bench response therefore needs its device and geometry context; it does not establish the frequency or severity of clinical events among people with implanted systems.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 3 to 4, Test protocol and Results; page 6, Discussion, in-vitro versus in-vivo comparison

t05.title: Read monitor modes separately from infant outcomes

paragraphs.text: The FOPH fact sheet distinguishes sound-triggered transmission from short signals used to check whether the parent unit remains within range. It also separates dedicated monitor links from network cameras and phone-based arrangements. A silent nursery therefore does not by itself describe the radio activity of every monitor. The equipment’s actual communication mode and the roles of both units belong with an emissions claim, while advanced monitoring of bodily functions lies outside this fact sheet’s scope.
paragraphs.locator: Held FOPH PDF physical page 1, device categories, automatic voice activation, range checks and scope

paragraphs.text: The adult crossover pilot used modified baby-monitor units and recorded several kinds of sleep outcome. Subjective scores and selected EEG differences appeared alongside nonsignificant comparisons for other measures, with differing available samples. Its discussion identifies limitations in transferring the signal to other device types.
